accepted.rationale: Test whether explicitly valuing an intact advancing Cat formation and zero escape routes separates genuinely winning traps from positions that merely look contained.

cats_win_forecast.instructions: Who wins with correct play, using the measured Cat formation {{cat_front_row}}, {{cat_rear_row}}, {{cat_row_spread}}, {{cat_count_left_behind}}, {{front_row_gap}}, {{cat_adjacent_pairs}}, Mouse position {{mouse_row}}, current mobility {{mouse_mobility}}, covered exits {{covered_mouse_moves}}, and safe monotone routes {{mouse_routes}}?

criteria.cats_win: The Cats can force a trap before the Mouse reaches row 0 or gets above every Cat; the conclusion remains valid despite any current free move.
criteria.mouse_win: The Mouse has a forced route to row 0 or above all Cats, or the Cat formation leaves an unavoidable escape lane that prevents a forced trap.
criteria.draw: Neither side has a demonstrated forced result from this position.

mouse_containment.instructions: Is the Mouse actually contained rather than merely having few current moves, given {{mouse_mobility}}, {{covered_mouse_moves}}, {{mouse_routes}}, {{mouse_row}}, and the Cat front-to-rear structure {{cat_row_spread}}?

criteria.cats_win: All relevant paths toward row 0 are blocked or can be closed while the Cats retain a connected formation; safe monotone routes are zero and no persistent escape lane remains.
criteria.mouse_win: The Mouse owns a safe route or can use an uncovered diagonal to pass the Cats before they can close it; current mobility or route count reveals a durable escape.
criteria.draw: The Mouse is restricted but the available evidence does not establish either a forced trap or a forced escape.

cat_formation.instructions: How strategically strong is the Cats' own formation for blocking the Mouse, using front row {{cat_front_row}}, rear row {{cat_rear_row}}, row spread {{cat_row_spread}}, Cats left behind {{cat_count_left_behind}}, front-row gap {{front_row_gap}}, and adjacent pairs {{cat_adjacent_pairs}}?
criteria: The Cats are fragmented: large row spread, stranded or left-behind Cats, major front-row gaps, and little useful adjacency; the Mouse can exploit the broken formation.
The Cats have substantial fragmentation or a dangerous gap, with only partial adjacency and weak coverage of the Mouse side.
The formation is mixed: some Cats cooperate, but spacing, gaps, or a rear Cat leave an uncertain blocking structure.
The Cats are mostly connected and advance with limited spread or gaps; any rear Cat still contributes to closing the Mouse.
The Cats form a compact advancing barrier: nearly all Cats share the front line, no Cat is stranded, gaps are closed, and diagonal adjacency preserves coverage.

cat_front_row.name: front row
cat_front_row.definition: the row of the most advanced Cat

cat_rear_row.name: rear row
cat_rear_row.definition: the row of the least advanced Cat

cat_row_spread.name: row spread
cat_row_spread.definition: max(cat row) minus min(cat row): how far the line has stretched lengthwise

cat_count_left_behind.name: cats left behind
cat_count_left_behind.definition: how many Cats are NOT on the front row (4 minus cats_on_front_row)

front_row_gap.name: gap in the front row
front_row_gap.definition: the longest run of empty dark squares between two Cats of the front row (0 when fewer than two Cats are there); dark squares on one row are two columns apart

cat_adjacent_pairs.name: adjacent Cat pairs
cat_adjacent_pairs.definition: how many pairs of Cats touch diagonally (a chain of four has three, a tight block more)

mouse_row.name: Mouse row
mouse_row.definition: the Mouse row: 0 is its goal, 7 is its start

mouse_mobility.name: Mouse mobility
mouse_mobility.definition: how many legal moves the Mouse has right now

covered_mouse_moves.name: covered Mouse exits
covered_mouse_moves.definition: how many of the Mouse legal moves land on a square the Cats attack

mouse_routes.name: Mouse routes
mouse_routes.definition: how many distinct monotone paths the Mouse has from its square to row 0 (one row up per step, dark squares only) that avoid every square the Cats attack; the count stops at `cap`
